title: Localization at units, or at a set containing 0
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $T\subseteq R$ a multiplicative subset ($1\in T$, $st\in T$ for $s,t\in T$). Let $\lambda:R\to R'$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings which is a localization of $R$ at $T$: (a) $\lambda(t)$ is a unit for every $t\in T$; (b) every element of $R'$ is $\lambda(r)\lambda(t)^{-1}$ with $r\in R$, $t\in T$; (c) $\lambda(r)=0$ implies $tr=0$ for some $t\in T$ (for instance $R'=T^{-1}R$, the ring of fractions $r/t$, with $\lambda(r)=r/1$). Then (1) $R'$ is the zero ring if and only if $0\in T$; (2) if every element of $T$ is a unit of $R$, then $\lambda$ is an isomorphism of rings (so $R'\cong R$ as $R$-algebras).

source.place: (1) Lemma Tag 00CQ (algebra-lemma-localization-zero, line 1111); (2) from the universal property, Proposition Tag 00CP (algebra-proposition-universal-property-localization, line 1083): the identity of R inverts T, giving g with g(λ(r))=r, and λ(g(r/t))=λ(r t^{-1})=r/t

localization at a submonoid consisting of units is an isomorphism R ≃ S
localization of a ring at a submonoid of units is isomorphic to the ring itself
